run.question:
EU prod is having a checkout incident — 500s on POST /api/checkout. Investigate
using the app-267-prod-logs index.

report.summary: The app-267-prod-logs documents self-identify as cluster acme-prod-eu-west-1, environment prod, region eu-west-1, so this log index matches the EU prod checkout incident. That index holds exactly four documents in the authorized window (2026-11-20T06:36:54Z to 2026-11-21T06:36:54Z), and they describe one chain: at 2026-11-21T04:36:45Z checkout-service logged 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (adyen-eu)' and payment-service logged 'Upstream timeout calling adyen-eu /v68/payments after 30000ms'; at 05:36:45Z checkout-service logged 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 36%)'; at 06:06:45Z payment-service warned 'adyen-eu degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=620'. The deepest cause the evidence supports is the external payment provider adyen-eu timing out / degrading; payment-service and checkout-service failures (including the open circuit breaker) follow from it. Note that the log line reports a failed POST /api/checkout but does not itself carry an HTTP status code, so '500' is not directly confirmed by these documents. The Kubernetes/Prometheus target I could read is a different cluster: its own objects and rules identify it as opsk.../opspilot-m1 (node opspilot-m1-control-plane, alerting rule label cluster: opspilot-m1, namespace otel-demo); its checkout (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout) and payment (…-payment) pods are 1/1 ready with healthy endpoints and its checkout logs show successful payments at 04:54:41Z and 05:56:08Z, so nothing from that cluster is used as evidence of, or impact for, the acme-prod-eu-west-1 incident. Metrics and traces could not be used at all: every Prometheus and Jaeger query in this Run returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE.

claims.text: Index app-267-prod-logs has docs.count=4 and maps the fields cluster, environment, level, message, region, service and timestamp (timestamp is the date field; the index does not map @timestamp).

The whole 24-hour window query on app-267-prod-logs returned exactly 4 documents, all with cluster=acme-prod-eu-west-1, environment=prod, region=eu-west-1; service values are checkout-service (2 documents) and payment-service (2 documents), levels ERROR (3) and WARN (1), timestamps 2026-11-21T04:36:45Z (two), 05:36:45Z and 06:06:45Z.
checkout-service ERROR at 2026-11-21T04:36:45Z: 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (adyen-eu)' (cluster acme-prod-eu-west-1, environment prod).
payment-service ERROR at the same second 2026-11-21T04:36:45Z: 'Upstream timeout calling adyen-eu /v68/payments after 30000ms' (cluster acme-prod-eu-west-1).
checkout-service ERROR at 2026-11-21T05:36:45Z: 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 36%)' — an hour after the adyen-eu timeout line.
payment-service WARN at 2026-11-21T06:06:45Z: 'adyen-eu degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=620'.

The fault originates at the external payment provider adyen-eu, which the acme-prod-eu-west-1 logs name as the upstream that timed out after 30000ms on /v68/payments at 04:36:45Z and as being in 'degraded mode' at 06:06:45Z; payment-service and checkout-service failures (the checkout 'POST /api/checkout failed' error and the circuit breaker open for payment-service) are downstream of this provider.

The Kubernetes/Prometheus target readable in this Run is a different cluster, self-identified as opsk.../opspilot-m1: node opspilot-m1-control-plane, and the Prometheus alerting rule CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh in namespace otel-demo carries the label cluster: opspilot-m1. That cluster's otel-demo deployments checkout (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout) and payment (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment) are each 1/1 ready with Services checkout and payment backed by ready endpoints (10.244.0.12:8080 and 10.244.0.17:8080).

In the opspilot-m1 lab cluster, no adyen-eu Service or workload exists (cluster services matching adyen|payment|checkout are only otel-demo/checkout:8080 and otel-demo/payment:8080), so the provider named in the acme-prod-eu-west-1 logs is external to that cluster and has no Kubernetes object I could inspect there.

The opspilot-m1 lab cluster does not reproduce this failure: its checkout pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n logged '[PlaceOrder] user_id=...' at 04:33:07Z, 'payment went through (transaction_id: …)' at 04:54:41Z and 05:56:08Z, and 'order confirmation email sent' at 05:34:34Z, with no error/exception/timeout/circuit lines among the returned matches; therefore its healthy checkout/payment pods are not evidence about, or impact of, the acme-prod-eu-west-1 incident.

In the opspilot-m1 lab cluster every otel-demo pod carries a last termination with exit code 255, reason Unknown, finishedAt 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z (one restart each), and metrics-server, local-path-provisioner and prometheus-readonly-proxy show exit codes 1/2 with 2-3 restarts; that cluster-wide restart coincides in time with, but has no evidenced connection to, the acme-prod-eu-west-1 errors.

The prometheus-readonly-proxy pod prometheus-readonly-proxy-f4866f767-62bgn in opspilot-m1 namespace otel-demo had a previous container exit at 2026-11-21T04:24:10Z with 'nginx: [emerg] host not found in upstream "prometheus:9090" in /etc/nginx/nginx.conf:22', which is a plausible reason metrics queries through that proxy path failed during this Run (its current container produced no log lines in the window).

checkout-service's circuit-breaker/failure-rate threshold (36% failure rate observed at 05:36:45Z) turns partial payment-service failures into full 'POST /api/checkout' failures; its configuration could not be read for the acme-prod-eu-west-1 cluster, so this amplification remains a hypothesis rather than a second root cause.

payment-service's growing retry queue (depth=620 reported at 06:06:45Z) may have prolonged recovery after adyen-eu degraded, but no queue or retry metric was obtainable, so the extent and duration of that backlog are unverified.

Fault-injection flags named for this service are not supported as the cause by what I could read: the only flagd configuration available (otel-demo/flagd-config in the opspilot-m1 lab cluster) keeps paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable at defaultVariant 'off', and no flagd or payment fault setting for the acme-prod-eu-west-1 cluster was readable; the acme-prod-eu-west-1 log text instead names an upstream provider timeout.

Obtain the adyen-eu provider status-page/incident timeline for 2026-11-21 04:00-06:10Z to confirm when the 30s /v68/payments timeouts began and cleared, and ask the provider for the request IDs behind the 04:36:45Z timeouts.

Review checkout-service's circuit-breaker/retry policy toward payment-service and payment-service's provider timeout and retry-queue settings, since an open circuit breaker on a 36% failure rate converts a partial dependency failure into failed checkouts.

Restore Prometheus metrics and Jaeger trace access for the acme-prod-eu-west-1 target (all Prometheus/Jaeger queries in this Run returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE) so the checkout error rate and the CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh rule state can be measured instead of inferred.

gaps: Prometheus and Jaeger were unavailable: get_all_labels, traces_search, traces_list_services (x2), get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query (x2), metrics_range_query and list_prometheus_rules all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate, latency, queue-depth or span evidence exists for checkout-service/payment-service and the 36% failure rate and '500' status are not independently confirmed.

Kubernetes object access covered only the opspilot-m1 lab cluster (namespace otel-demo, node opspilot-m1-control-plane; alert rule label cluster: opspilot-m1); no objects for cluster acme-prod-eu-west-1 (checkout-service, payment-service) were readable, so their pod status, events, resources, network policies and provider configuration are unknown.

app-267-prod-logs contains only 4 documents in the 24-hour window (04:36:45Z, 04:36:45Z, 05:36:45Z, 06:06:45Z); onset before 04:36, current state after 06:06:45Z, request/error counts and affected-customer scope are unknown, and the log lines do not state the HTTP status code of the failed POST /api/checkout.

Whether the acme-prod-eu-west-1 cluster has any fault-injection or provider-simulation setting (for example a flagd equivalent) could not be checked, and the adyen-eu provider itself is external with no telemetry available; its degradation is known only through the two payment-service log lines and the referenced status page.

Events in the window reference a Deployment checkout and a Deployment loki in namespace app-282 (ScalingReplicaSet 0 to 1 at 06:35:13-14Z, SuccessfulCreate, Scheduled, Started) and a Running/Ready pod app-282/checkout-698c8f5df-6fwl5 (python:3.9-slim plus promtail sidecars, 0 restarts), yet the deployments query returned no app-282 deployments (namespace query returned no_data); these changes came after all incident log lines and could not be placed as affected or explained, so they remain an unresolved observation.

Whether the opspilot-m1 lab cluster's container restart wave at 04:23:42Z (exit code 255, reason Unknown, plus metrics-server/local-path-provisioner/prometheus-readonly-proxy failures) is what broke the Prometheus/Jaeger query path is a hypothesis; the lab Prometheus pod itself was still logging ingest activity through 06:35:49Z.
next_steps: Pull the adyen-eu provider incident/status timeline and per-request timeout logs for /v68/payments covering 2026-11-21 04:00-06:30Z.
Re-run the checkout PlaceOrder error-ratio and payment latency queries once Prometheus and Jaeger are reachable for the acme-prod-eu-west-1 target.
Inspect checkout-service and payment-service pod status, events, resource limits, and their provider-URL/timeout/retry/circuit-breaker configuration in the acme-prod-eu-west-1 cluster.
Confirm with ingress or frontend-proxy access logs that POST /api/checkout actually returned HTTP 500 (and at what rate) during 04:36-06:10Z.

    client_auth:[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]      password: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]      username: collector
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  - basicauth/prometheus
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - otlphttp/prometheus
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - redis
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - otlp
      - debug
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - periodic:
          exporter:
            otlp:
              endpoint: otel-collector:4318
              protocol: grpc
          interval: 10000
          timeout: 5000
"}

{"alerting_rules.yml":"groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind.
